title.narrative: SMHI Inception phase Climate Resilient Development

description.narrative: The objective of an Inception phase is to allow SMHI time and resources to complete information needed in their original proposal in regards to the following: 1. Include a description of long term results beyond the ouputs and describe the possibility for upscaling of the program with financing from other sources. 2. Detail the budget to allow for Sida to judge the effectiveness and efficiency of the program 3. Describe the target groups and countries to be included in the program and why they were chosen. Limit the number of countries and deepen the analysis of the country analysis. Identify different actors and their role in the program and the connection to the overall goals of the program 4. The local connections and partners need to be described and the ToC needs to be connected to the local context which includes the local perspective and promotes local ownership (in the form of decision making and strategic choices.) 5. A clear risk assessment in relation to the conflict perspective and power balance needs to be included. 6. Focus areas in different sectors such as agriculture and urban planning should be include. 7. Synergies with other ongoing programs should be explored. 8. An environmental assessment should be included. 9. Strategic results frameworks and how this will be followed up should be developed.

Programmet "Klimat Resiliens Utveckling för Afrika" fokuserar på att stärka den institutionella kapaciteten för en långsiktigt hållbar klimatanpassning. Genom analys och användning av klimatdata och klimatmodellering målet är för ett mer hållbar klimatanpassad planering och beslut inom viktiga sektorer som infrastruktur, jordbruk och katastrofförebyggande verktyg (Early Warning Systems (EWS)). I inledningsfasen kommer SMHI att knyta närmare kontakter med lokala partners och utveckla ett lokalt kontextbaserat kapacitetsutvecklingsprogram som främjar användningen av klimatdata i programplaneringen inom alla sektorer.

The programme "Climate Resilient Development for Africa" focuses on strengthening institutional capacity for a long-term sustainable climate adaptation, by the analysis and use of climate data and climate modeling for more sustainable climate adapted planning and decisions in important sectors such as infrastructure, agriculture, and disaster prevention tools (Early Warning Systems (EWS)). In the Inception phase, SMHI will connect more closely with local partners and develop a locally context based capacity development program which promotes the use of climate data in program planning in all sectors.

15 program rounds completed - 375 participants received training in climate change, - 308 Change projects implemented, - 22 facilitators trained in coaching, - 10 alumni networks established, - 28 Case studies in English and French (https://www.smhi.se/en/climate/education/capacitydevelopment/international-training-programmes/case-studies-1.191536(. - Various articles and films published on the ITP website for awareness raising in Sweden and internationally. Program information available on SMHI website: International Training Programmes | SMHI)
A few examples from the Change Projects:
- The Zambia Disaster Management and Mitigation unit uses Cordex data from the training program (ITP 309) to guide disaster prevention and preparedness.
- New guidelines on Climate smart road building in Rwanda allows farmers and others to travel to market more safely by building roads specifically adapted to local climate conditions (such as drainage for extreme rains, protection against landslides, etc).
- Integration of climate change parameters in agricultural insurance assisted farmers and government in Kenya save money and crops.
- Participants from the meteorology, hydrology and disaster risk reduction units in Zambia developed a concept note for a flood early warning project in a remote part of Zambia. The project idea was presented to the local Sida office and is seeking financing. This is only one example of how participants now able to write and submit program proposals which have potential for financing and which are focused on local action.
- In Kenya proposed training for Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation program for Makueni County and in Migori County Change Project 'training of trainers' in climate mitigation and adaptation activities for local climate committees has received funding. 20 Trainers received training and in turn have held seminars on Climate Change adaptation tactics with over 200 Climate committee and local plans now integrated with climate adaptation.
- Introduction of climate and climate smart agriculture into curriculum and school activities in Zambia and Zimbabwe to create a climate smart next generation. "The recognition we got is great motivation for us to keep on and up-scale our change project as well as develop more of such projects which will contribute to climate change resilience efforts at community, national, regional and global level. ITP have successfully inspired a young generation that will actively participate in addressing the global problem of Climate Change."
- Development and implementation of an efficient cyclone early warning system in Zimbabwe saves lives and property.
- The operational flood forecasting system and alerts in West Africa (FANFAR) started as a participant's Change Project is implemented. 9 countries around the Niger River Basin work together with AGRYMET, the regional network of climate and meteorological organisations, coordinates the program. An estimated 2000 lives and property saved in the region from the most devastating flood effects in 2021.
- 8 of the program's alumni actively participated at UNCFFF, (United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change) and at the CoP 26 and CoP 27 (Climate Change Conference of the Parties).
- Changing attitudes and practices takes time, for example Musawa Musonda Hamusonde organised funding to plant 2000 indigenous trees in and around the Victoria Falls World Heritage Site on the Zambian side of the border. As a pilot, the expected long-term impact is that the project will inspire others to plant trees and additional carbon sinks will help to reinforce the resilience of the site to the negative impacts of climate change and also mitigate them. Also the reintroduction of indigenous species restores the aesthetics and ecological integrity and biodiversity of the site.
- An ITP alumni initiated a program which helps women and girls to engage in the protection of Natural Resources as well as Climate Smart Agricultural related activities, and that enables them to improve their livelihoods with the income generated from their businesses. The project also worked with increasing institutional capacity of the government office for Climate Change and Agricultural Service Providers better enabling the government office in its support of women farmers. As community members became aware of and active in the project's cause, the integrated approach helped to realize their aspirations on addressing Climate Change and gender issues. The alumni of the ITP is now Executive Directress of the Union of Ethiopian Women and Children Associations (UEWCA).
- After the ITP training, participants from Botswana and Mozambique kept in touch and developed a concept note on how to contribute effectively in their region on climate change issues. They formed and registered a climate focused NGO in Mozambique where there is the greatest crisis and greatest opportunity to contribute in the region. The NGO which hopes to operate regionally in the future is called BREWEC Africa which stands for - Biodiversity, Resilience, Environment, Water, Ecosystems, and Climate.
The ITP Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation participants have successfully fund raised for their Change Projects, while SMHI has also received EU funding for the "FANFAR" Change Project in West Africa and funding for an inception phase for a new program, Climate Resilient Development for Africa (CRD4A), based on the origianl ITP program, but broadening the scope and focusing on the practical use of climate data in areas such as Smart Agriculture, Infrastructure and Urban Planning, and Disaster Risk Reduction.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
